source.title: Mitigating Measurement-Induced Training Instability in Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks for Protein Classification
source.authors: Milton Mondal; Sushovan Chanda; Mohamad Mahdi Alawieh; Brijesh Sukhadiya; Donatus Krah; Clinton Gonsalves; Antonios Ntolkeras; Silvio O. Rizzoli; Ali H. Shaib

record.tranche_reason: Reports gradient-based training outcomes for hybrid quantum neural networks, an extension to a different model setting from the versions’ classical-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training accuracy and gradient variance for its own QNN experiments. Results cited from other papers are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests a measurement-output scaling method for hybrid quantum classifiers. None of its results tests or relies on V1–V6: it does not examine the specified classical-network training-error, width, depth, initialization, stability-threshold, or batch-normalization comparisons. A different model setting alone does not establish a T3 test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute suppressed gradients and training instability to bounded measurement logits interacting with the loss, and conclude that jointly learned QMT improves optimization, accuracy, and stability without changing the quantum circuit. Their broader claims about other tasks are prospective rather than experimentally established.
record.recipe_differences: Hybrid quantum-classical neural-network training with a learned output-temperature intervention; the listed versions concern classical neural networks or two-layer ReLU teacher-student models.
record.method_sensitivity: QMT setting, dataset, architecture configuration, optimizer, batch size, learning rate, entanglement scheme, and training-stabilization method.

fits_no_version.finding: For CF=2, QB=6, QL=4, learned QMT raises mean training accuracy from 81.78% to 92.06% on protein images and from 84.74% to 90.74% on Fashion MNIST. Trial variability decreases, particularly on protein images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning measurement-output temperature improves training accuracy and can reduce variability in the tested hybrid quantum classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.5 reports gradient variance around 0.01 without QMT and more than tenfold higher variance with QMT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned measurement-output temperature increases parameter-gradient variance in the tested hybrid quantum classifiers.

record.problems: The text reports five independent trials and mean ± standard deviation for the tabulated outcomes, but the gradient-variance result is figure-based and lacks an exact value for the QMT condition. The experiments use statevector simulations.
record.rows_left_out: Other separately reported training-accuracy settings in Tables 1–3 and figures are not extracted; they concern the same hybrid-QNN result and do not test a listed version. The source also reports test accuracy, which does not measure training error.

untested.parts: Training-error outcomes for sufficiently large classical convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation in plain convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Initialization comparisons, activation matching, signal propagation, and initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature reduction, and edge-of-stability dynamics. The learning-rate sweep reports test accuracy without such measurements.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All five rows concern findings outside V1–V6 and should not serve as evidence for verdicts on those versions. The analytical bound on cross-entropy loss concerns confidence and loss, not a necessary floor on classification error. No omitted result in the supplied text warrants a missing entry for a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test classical convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or the stated model-size and training-duration conditions.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or neuron-width sweep.
No plain-versus-residual classical network depth comparison.
Does not compare initialization schemes or test trainable depth by initialization.
Does not test learning rates above a stability threshold or measure sharpness.
Does not compare batch normalization with no normalization.

rows.note: The text describes the value as too low when QMT is not used; corresponding QMT variance is described as more than 10 times higher but not numerically specified.
rows.check: The approximate variance is stated in Section 6.5 but does not test activation-matched initialization or any other listed mechanism. The protein-only condition is ambiguous: Figure 7 labels both Protein Dataset and Fashion MNIST panels, while its caption refers to protein classification.
